one_month_reasoning: No Snowflake earnings in the window: Q3 FY27 is expected early December (Dec 2 is a data-vendor estimate, not a company announcement; Q3 FY26 was reported Dec 3, 2025). In-window items: (1) the $3.75B 0% convertible closes Oct 1; the pricing and convert-arb hedging hit the tape Sep 28-29 and are in the price; (2) the Oct 13 motion-to-dismiss filing in the newer class action (a filing, not a ruling) and a possible ruling on the older action's MTD, both small valuation items; (3) the Oct 28-29 FOMC. My round-1 1-month ladder leaned slightly down on 67-69% prediction-market hike odds, but those readings (Kalshi 69.5c / Polymarket 68.5c on Sep 29) pre-date the Sep 30 August PCE print (core 3.0% vs 3.3% expected, headline 3.4% vs 3.7%), after which traders cut October hike odds (swaps ~36% per the supervisor's Bloomberg cite) and pushed the next hike to December. With rate risk now two-sided, I remove the tilt: symmetric lognormal centred on spot $337.50 with ~16% monthly sigma (a bit under the 62%/3.5 = 17.7% rule because realized vol is inflated by the April 2026 crash and the Sep 3 +21% gap). Post-earnings drift (mildly up) and past-winner reversal / 5% short interest (chop) roughly cancel.

fair_value.method: Blend of EV/NTM revenue (12.5x on ~$9.6B NTM revenue at Sep-2027 = $120B EV + ~$1.9B Sep-2027 net cash, / 388M diluted shares = $314) and forward P/E (FY29E non-GAAP EPS ~$4.15 x 75x = $311), weighted 60/40. Down from $320 in round 1 because net cash after the new $3.75B convert, capped calls and in-the-money 2027-note repurchase is ~$1B lower and share count ~3M higher.

methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Sep-2027 ~$9.6B x 12.5x = $120B EV + ~$1.9B net cash = $121.9B / 388M diluted shares

inputs_detail.derivation: Product revenue guide $6,070M; total revenue ~4.5% above product per Q2 mix ($1.55B total vs $1.49B product).
Remaining ~4 months of FY28 at consensus run-rate plus 8 months of FY29 at ~24% growth off $8.11B (~$10.05B); time-weighted ~$9.6B. Supervisor's check agrees (~$9.5-9.8B).

Today ~16x forward (TIKR, top of 3-yr range); LTM EV/rev compressed 32.9x (2024) -> 25x (2025) -> 20.3x LTM, a steady ~20%/yr de-rating; peer line (DDOG 10.6x at 20%, PLTR 44.9x at 63%) implies ~12-13x for mid-20s growth. I stay at 12.5x rather than the supervisor's 13x centre: the base rate of annual compression plus Databricks (company-reported >$7B run-rate, >80% y/y, now larger and growing >2x faster) argues against the upper half of the band.

Jul-31-2026 cash+ST+LT investments $4.33B + ~$3.71B net convert proceeds - $0.38B capped calls - $0.55B 2027-note repurchase = ~$7.1B, vs ~$5.8B face debt ($2.30B old notes less ~$0.26B face repurchased, since they convert at $157.50 and are ~2.1x in the money, plus $3.75B new) = ~$1.3B pro forma; plus ~$1.6B NTM adj. FCF less ~$0.65B RSU tax withholding and ~$0.35B buybacks = ~$1.9B.

Q3 guide 382M non-GAAP diluted; ~5M net excess shares from the in-the-money 2024 notes after capped calls ($157.50-$225) that are not all in the guide; ~1% net SBC dilution partly offset by buybacks. New notes ($484/$500 conversion) are out of the money.

Consensus $3.02 grown ~39% (~24% revenue growth plus ~2pt non-GAAP margin expansion per year; guide raised 13.5%->14.5%, Q3 15.5%) = $4.20, trimmed ~1% for the higher 388M share count; 0% coupons add no interest cost, but lower interest income on cash used for capped calls/repurchase.
Stock trades ~132x NTM EPS today (TIKR); margins are still ramping so P/E compresses as EPS grows faster than price; 75x ~ 3x a ~25% growth rate, typical for top-decile growth software.

bear.story: Growth decelerates back to ~20% as the AI consumption tailwind normalises, share loss to Databricks (>$7B run-rate, >80% growth) shows up in NRR, or AI-disintermediation fears return (as in the Apr-2026 56% drawdown); with a 10-year near 5% the multiple resets to ~8x NTM sales, near the early-2026 trough. SNOW has done this twice: -70% after the Nov-2021 peak and -56% into Apr-2026. (Round 1's 'Fed hikes in Oct/Dec' element dropped: October hike odds fell after the Sep 30 PCE print.)

base.story: Product growth holds mid/high-30s near term, fading to mid-20s by FY29; revenue compounds ~28% but the multiple compresses from ~16x to ~12.5-13x, and net cash is only ~$2B after the new converts, so price is roughly flat to slightly down; fair value ~$313-330.

bull.story: Further acceleration, AI products (Cortex, agents) become a visible revenue line, FY28 guide at 30%+; multiple holds ~15-16x on ~$10B NTM revenue; the new convert cash funds buybacks/M&A; approaches the $484/$500 conversion prices and the upper half of analyst targets ($414 mean / $525 high).

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$210 (about -38%, ~8.5x NTM sales, back under the pre-Q2-earnings breakout zone) the market would be saying the reacceleration was a one-off: product growth sliding back toward 20%, NRR falling from 126% toward 115-120%, or visible share loss to Databricks/AI agents. That is beyond ordinary 1-sigma volatility over a few months and should coincide with a guide-down at the Q3 (Dec) or Q4 (Feb/Mar) print. Caveat from the base rates: a macro software liquidation took the stock to $118 in April 2026 without a fundamental break, so confirm with the fundamentals. Lowered $5 from round 1 in line with the ~$7 lower fair value.

reasoning: Round 2. Anchor unchanged: SNOW's own history has extreme two-way base rates (-70% after the Nov-2021 peak, -56% into Apr-2026, then a round-trip to new highs with a +21% gap on Q2 FY27: product +37%, FY guide $6.07B/+36%, NRR 126%). Realized vol 62% is inflated by those shocks; I use ~40-50% effective forward vol via a three-component mixture. Valuation base rate: LTM EV/rev compressed every year (32.9x, 25x, ~20x; ~16x forward now), so ~28% revenue growth is mostly eaten by de-rating to ~12.5x. Supervisor corrections I accept after checking the pricing release: the $3.75B 0% convert (conversion $484/$500, $383.5M capped calls capped at $820, $548M to repurchase in-the-money 2027 notes) leaves pro forma net cash ~$1.3B, ~$1.9B by Sep-2027, not ~$3B; with ~388M shares that cuts fair value from $320 to $313. I keep 12.5x rather than the supervisor's 13x (base-rate compression plus Databricks' >80% growth at larger scale). The Oct FOMC hike odds I cited (Kalshi 69.5c/Polymarket 68.5c, Sep 29, via aggregator) were stale after the cooler Sep 30 PCE (core 3.0% vs 3.3% expected), so I removed the downward rate tilt from the 1-month ladder and the Fed-hike element from the bear story; the 12-month rate headwind is smaller but not gone (December hike still favoured). Scenario mix: bear $185 (22%), base $325 (53%), bull $475 (25%); mean ~$332, median ~$333, so P(>=338) slips to 0.48 from 0.495 and the ladder shifts down ~1-1.5 points through the middle. Research this round was 4 queries (convert pricing, prediction-market odds, PCE reaction); I could not reach a live Polymarket/Kalshi quote after the PCE print, so the post-PCE October odds rest on the supervisor's Bloomberg swaps figure plus CNBC's report that traders cut October hike odds.
